name: Artemis IV
first: First crewed lunar landing since Apollo 17 (1972)
description: Since NASA's February 2026 change of plan, Artemis IV is the mission that returns people to the lunar surface — the first landing since Apollo 17 in 1972, and the first ever near the south pole. SLS, on its last flight with the interim upper stage, launches Orion with four crew towards the Moon. In lunar orbit they meet a commercial lander — SpaceX's Starship or Blue Origin's Blue Moon, chosen after the Artemis III docking tests — and two astronauts descend to the south polar region for about a week of surface work, while two remain aboard Orion. The south pole is the target because its permanently shadowed craters hold water ice, which future missions may turn into drinking water, oxygen and rocket propellant. NASA has identified nine candidate landing regions. Planned for early 2028; the crew has not yet been named.

events.label: SLS LAUNCH
events.note: Orion launches from KSC LC-39B with crew of 4.

events.label: NRHO ARRIVAL
events.note: Orion arrives in a high lunar orbit and meets the waiting lander.

events.label: DESCENT
events.note: 2 crew transfer to the lander; powered descent to the lunar south pole.

events.label: ASCENT
events.note: The lander returns to lunar orbit after about a week of surface operations.

events.label: SPLASHDOWN
events.note: Orion splashes down in the Pacific Ocean.
